route: Storage first, then the jobs that use it, the email they send, the API contract and the endpoint behind its Retry link, and the button that calls it. Tests sit next to the code they cover.

f1.what: Adds attempts, last_error and failed_at to order_syncs, plus a partial index on failed_at.
f1.why: Start here: every other file reads or writes these columns.

f2.what: Splits the old errored status into retrying and failed, and adds record_failure! and retry!.
f2.why: The job, the controller and the UI all call into this model.

f3.what: Covers the attempt limit and the retrying branch.
f3.why: Sits beside the model it tests.

f4.what: Failures now go through record_failure!, and retrying syncs are enqueued again with backoff.
f4.why: The first caller of the model methods you just read.

f5.what: Checks the job enqueues itself again with backoff.
f5.why: Sits beside the job it tests.

f6.what: New job that sends each shop one digest of the syncs that failed in the last 24 hours.
f6.why: Uses failed_since from the model and hands off to the mailer.

f7.why: The only thing that runs the digest job.

f8.what: Adds the failure_digest email, sent to the shop owner.

f9.what: Email template: one row per failed order, each with a Retry link into the admin.
f9.why: Its Retry link is what the new route serves.

f10.what: English copy for the digest subject and the retry notice.
f10.why: Read after the mailer that uses its subject key.

f11.what: Adds the retry operation to the admin API and the new fields on OrderSync.
f11.why: The contract. The OpenAPI file and the zod client are generated from it.

f16.why: The entry point for the Retry button and the email link.

f17.what: Only admins and the shop owner may retry.
f17.why: Read before the controller that authorizes against it.

f18.what: New retry action: authorize, call retry!, answer as JSON or redirect.
f18.why: Joins the route, the policy and the model.

f19.what: Mirrors the new statuses and adds retrySync, which tracks in-flight retries.
f19.why: Calls the controller you just read.

f20.what: Failed syncs get a Retry button that shows a loading state while the retry runs.
f20.why: Last stop: what the shop owner sees.

f21.what: Status labels for the badge, including the new Retry button.
f21.why: Read after the badge that renders these labels.

hunks.f1.h1: New migration. The partial index only covers failed rows.
hunks.f2.h1: Enum value 2 changes from errored to retrying, so existing errored rows will read as retrying.
hunks.f2.h2: record_failure! counts attempts and gives up at five. retry! resets the sync and enqueues it again.
hunks.f3.h1: Two cases for record_failure!. retry! has no test yet.
hunks.f4.h1: Adds retry_on for rate limits and its own retry loop for other errors.
hunks.f5.h1: One case: a 502 on the second attempt re-enqueues after 4 minutes.
hunks.f6.h1: New file. Queries failed syncs once per shop and delivers later.
hunks.f7.h1: Solid Queue recurring task. Runs in the server's time zone.
hunks.f8.h1: Subject comes from the locale file and counts the failed orders.
hunks.f9.h1: last_error is nullable, so .truncate can raise on a nil error.
hunks.f10.h1: Pluralized subject, plus the flash notice the controller shows.
hunks.f11.h1: Retry can answer 404 and 403. The status union matches the model enum.
hunks.f16.h1: Member route on the existing admin syncs resource.
hunks.f17.h1: Narrower than show?, which also lets staff in.
hunks.f18.h1: Nothing checks that the sync is failed before retrying it.
hunks.f19.h1: Type now matches the model enum.
hunks.f19.h2: Optimistic retrying flag, cleared when the response lands. No error path.
hunks.f20.h1: Button only appears for failed, not for retrying.
hunks.f21.h1: Drops the errored label and adds retrying, failed and retry.
